reading_note:
Ledger row 1 asked for the dense masked LOSS's share of step time. It stays at 0.7-3.0 percent in every cell, never above 9.6 ms, and is always smaller than the `lm_head_projection` that feeds it logits -- so it is not a principal cost in this fixture. (An earlier draft called it the smallest operation in every cell, which is wrong: `noising` is smaller in 7 of 8, and `loss` is smallest only at 32K/2L/B=1.) The Unsloth Triton CE it wraps is not where this step's time goes. What the loss row's neighbour costs instead is the LM-HEAD PROJECTION that feeds it: 6.5 to 26.7 percent, and 84.2 ms at V=128256/B=32, driven by the [B, L, V] logits GEMM rather than the cross-entropy over it. Separating `lm_head_projection` from `loss` is what made that visible; a single fused 'loss' event would have reported up to 29.7 percent and pointed at the wrong operation.

Backward dominates once batch leaves 1 (53.6-66.2 percent), and `optimizer_step` repeats the ELF pattern exactly: its absolute cost is batch-invariant (3.83/3.84/3.83 ms at 32K; 13.71/13.80/13.75 ms at 128256), so its share collapses from 47.7 to 3.7 percent as batch grows. Reading only B=1 would name the optimizer the hot path and be wrong for any realistic batch -- the same trap the ELF cell set.

Vocabulary is the decisive axis for the LM head, and NOT monotonically in batch: the 128256-over-32000 step ratio is 2.8x at B=1, 3.6x at B=8 and 3.1x at B=32.

The 8-layer sensitivity cell earns its place. Quadrupling depth raises the step only 2.3x (24.35 -> 56.83 ms at 32K/B=8) because the LM head and loss are depth-invariant, so a 2-layer fixture OVERSTATES the LM head's share: 15.1 percent at 2 layers falls to 7.3 percent at 8. Any share quoted from this artifact must name its depth.

Stage-1 profile only. No target is selected; Stage 2 owns that.
